note: `contradictory_evidence` became `conflicting_revisions` on 2026-08-26 and both it and `differing_evidence_is_not_contradiction` now target PASS. The rule they tested checked whether a claim cited two evidence items with differing text -- plurality, not contradiction -- and passed for the wrong reason. It is gone: no contradiction is decidable here without either the question's time scope (a semantic judgement, OPEN_DECISIONS D-11) or a corpus that declares which revision supersedes which (metadata revision_id does not carry). Conflicting revisions are reported by the verifier and shown to the reader; nothing gates on them. Both cases exist so that stays visible in the benchmark rather than being mistaken for coverage.
